sub_niches: mythology and folklore verified sources only
target_audience: Adults 24-45, curious and educated, interested in history, documentaries, true crime, podcasts and books.

phase_1_bootstrap.note: Two daily slots target US afternoon and UK evening simultaneously.

phase_2_steady.note: Quality over quantity. This audience rewards depth and consistency more than volume.

schedule.longform_cadence: Every 4th topic as a 4-7 minute video using the same script expanded with context and atmosphere.

visual_style: Pure black backgrounds, deep crimson and burgundy accents, antique matte gold for highlights. Chiaroscuro lighting on a single subject. BBC documentary meets gothic woodcut illustration.
narration_notes: Deep, measured, slightly raspy. British or deep American narrative tone preferred. 130-150 wpm. Build tension before the reveal. Never rush the hook.
hook_strategy: Open with the most disturbing or baffling verified fact, then withhold the explanation. First sentence is the entire reason to watch.
competitor_channels: faceless channels reading Wikipedia verbatim with stock footage
low-effort top-10 history lists with no narrative
allowed_topics: forgotten plagues and mass hysteria events
mythology and folklore with historical basis
dark side of famous historical periods
forbidden_topics: glorification of totalitarian or genocidal regimes
gore without clear historical and educational context
content that could be used to promote violence

monetization.rpm_note: UK audience can push RPM higher. History/documentary niche can attract publishers and streaming advertisers.

secondary.cta_placement: End of every short and video description

ypp_target.watch_hours_or_views: 3M Shorts views OR 4000 longform watch hours

thumbnail_rules: Movie-still aesthetic with one disturbing or intriguing artifact in sharp focus
Heavy shadows: 70 percent of frame in darkness, subject lit dramatically from one side
Max 2-3 words as hook, ominous and provocative
Font mood: Cinzel or Playfair Display
No red arrows, no clickbait borders, no emoji
Aspect ratio strictly 16:9 for thumbnail and 9:16 for the short itself
brand.logo_description: A gothic hourglass with dark mist instead of sand, stylized in woodcut or etching art style. Antique matte gold on pure black.
example_video_titles: The strangest medieval weapon you've never heard of
Why this ancient village vanished from maps overnight
The Dancing Plague of 1518: They danced until they died
The real reason medieval people didn't bathe
He faked his own death and became a king
brand.sound_design_notes: Use a low ambient drone under narration, subtle reverb on voice, and period-appropriate sound effects such as quill scratching, distant church bell, and crackling fire.
brand.notes: Every claim must have a source. If uncertain, say 'some historians believe' rather than 'historians agree'. Credibility is the entire brand.

research.source_quality_requirement: Only topics verifiable through at least one academic or established journalistic source. Wikipedia is acceptable as starting point only.

june: bizarre summer festivals from the past

research.keyword_strategy: Mix evergreen deep-cuts with trending history hooks. Ratio: 70 percent evergreen, 30 percent topical.

qa_gate.narration_quality_check: Reject if audio sounds robotic or lacks tonal variation. Flag for manual review.
